title: Green beans, canned, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green beans are cooked beans packed in a sealed can with added fat to enhance flavor and texture. The product is ready to eat and is commonly used in salads, side dishes, and hot meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows the beans to be stored for 2–3 years without major loss of nutrients.
Added fat (usually vegetable oil) improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A and K present in the beans.
Green beans are high in dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.
Cans often indicate the country of origin – USA, Italy, China, etc.
Canned beans can be used in cold dishes without further cooking.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes normal digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Contains added plant fats
items.content: The added fats aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins and give a richer taste.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Even with added fat, canned green beans remain relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Fat quality
items.content: If the ingredient list includes trans fats or hydrogenated oils, consumption should be limited.

items.title: Microbial safety
items.content: Bulging or damaged cans may indicate bacterial growth and should not be consumed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drain the beans and eat them straight from the can, add them to salads, soups, stews, or casseroles. They can also be quickly warmed in a pan with extra seasonings if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator and use within 3–4 days.
